_meta.purpose: Complete dashboard modules. Each pattern carries its own selection metadata (intent / whenToUse / cardinality / alternatives) — there is no separate sections file.
_meta.levels: level "section" is placeable directly by a template slot; level "module" is embeddable inside another pattern and is reached via $ref. NOTE for dashboards: a "section"-level pattern is a ROW inside the page's single Section — it does NOT bring its own Section wrapper (see template.json → pageTypeSpecific.frame). That is what produces the bento look.

dashboard.page-header.purpose: Header row with the page title and the page-level action row.
dashboard.page-header.intent: Name the view and expose the actions that apply to the whole page.
dashboard.page-header.whenToUse: Always, exactly once, as the first row inside the Section.

dashboard.kpi-row.purpose: Three KPI cards in one row.
dashboard.kpi-row.intent: Show the headline figures of the view at a glance.
dashboard.kpi-row.whenToUse: The request names measurable values — counts, rates, totals, statuses. Use three cards; for four use the 25-25-25-25 grid, never more in one row.

dashboard.goal-row.purpose: Two goal cards with determinate progress.
dashboard.goal-row.whenToUse: The content is a target with a completion share and a deadline. Note the progress component only offers 25, 50 and 75 percent.

dashboard.filterbar.purpose: Search field on the left, filter and sort selects on the right.
dashboard.filterbar.whenToUse: The view shows a list or table the user must search, filter or sort. Uses the 33-33-33 grid with an empty middle column, exactly as captured. The search field carries the magnifier as a LEADING icon — that is what marks it as search rather than a plain text field.

dashboard.filter-tags.purpose: Row of removable tags representing the active filters.
dashboard.filter-tags.intent: Make the currently applied filters visible and removable.
dashboard.filter-tags.whenToUse: Filters are applied and the user must see and undo them. ALWAYS Tag (removable), never Badge — a Badge is a non-interactive status label. Emphasis is WEAK: the tags report the current state, they do not compete with the page actions; a strong tag row reads like a set of buttons.

dashboard.controls.purpose: Row combining the filter bar with the active-filter tags.
dashboard.controls.intent: Give the user control over the data set below.
dashboard.controls.whenToUse: A table or list panel follows and the user must narrow it down.

dashboard.table.purpose: Self-titled panel with a header row, divider-separated selectable rows and pagination below.
dashboard.table.intent: Show a selectable, paginated record set with aligned columns.
dashboard.table.whenToUse: The content is a record set the user selects, compares column by column or pages through. Use this instead of forcing a multi-column Grid.

dashboard.list-panel.purpose: Self-titled panel with a heading pair and divider-separated data rows, no selection.
dashboard.list-panel.intent: Show a read-only list of records under a titled surface.
dashboard.list-panel.whenToUse: A record set the user only reads and follows through a link — no selection, no pagination. Use dashboard.table when rows must be selectable.

dashboard.chart-card.purpose: Self-titled panel with a heading pair and a full-width row of chart bars with captions.
dashboard.chart-card.intent: Compare a handful of values visually.
dashboard.chart-card.whenToUse: Three to six comparable values where the shape matters more than the exact number. The bar row spans the FULL panel width — every bar fills its column, never a fixed bar width.

dashboard.charts.purpose: Two chart panels side by side.
dashboard.charts.intent: Put two comparable distributions next to each other.
dashboard.charts.whenToUse: The request asks for trends or distributions and two charts answer it. One chart alone belongs in a bento row beside another panel.

dashboard.bento-row.source: 1670:9239 Content Card + 1710:3211 Content Card - Bar Graph
dashboard.bento-row.purpose: Asymmetric row pairing a wide panel with a narrow one.
dashboard.bento-row.intent: Combine content of unequal weight in one row.
dashboard.bento-row.whenToUse: Two panels belong together but are not equivalent — e.g. a chart beside a goal card. This is the bento model; prefer it over repeating identical rows.
